USMLE-style practice · Clinical medicine

Urgent airway deterioration

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 15-year-old with a large peritonsillar swelling becomes increasingly distressed, drools continuously, and develops stridor. His voice is muffled and he cannot lie flat. Which action takes priority over obtaining a detailed diagnostic image?

  1. Urgent coordinated airway assessment by experienced clinicians
  2. Contrast CT before contacting the airway team
  3. IV antibiotics with reassessment after the first dose
  4. Bedside drainage without advanced airway support
  5. Nebulized epinephrine as the only intervention
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Urgent coordinated airway assessment by experienced clinicians

Signs of impending obstruction require early anesthesia/ENT involvement and airway planning before nonessential investigations.

Understanding the options

Urgent coordinated airway assessment by experienced clinicians
Signs of impending obstruction require early anesthesia/ENT involvement and airway planning before nonessential investigations.
Contrast CT before contacting the airway team
Imaging should not delay assessment of progressive stridor and inability to handle secretions.
IV antibiotics with reassessment after the first dose
Antibiotics are needed but will not reliably reverse an immediately threatened airway.
Bedside drainage without advanced airway support
Instrumentation risks worsening obstruction or aspiration in a patient with a precarious airway.
Nebulized epinephrine as the only intervention
A temporary effect on edema cannot replace expert assessment of a large infected space-occupying lesion.
